# Projection of Adobe-Japan1-7/cid2code.txt from cmap-resources 20231115:
# the CID and UniJIS-UTF32 columns, rows without a UniJIS-UTF32 value omitted.
# cid2code.txt (Version 05/18/2022)
#
# The data in this table contains 32 tab-delimited columns of
# information. The contents of this file supplement "The
# Adobe-Japan1-7 Character Collection":
#
# https://github.com/adobe-type-tools/Adobe-Japan1/
#
# This table contains lists CIDs 0 through 23059 in the first column,
# and provides additional columns that indicate whether a CID is used
# in a particular CMap file, and if so, provides the encoded
# value. Here are some common aspects of the data that you will find
# in this table:
#
# o All character codes are provided in hexadecimal notation.
#
# o Many of the CMap files indicated at the head of each column have
#   both "-H" (horizontal writing mode) and "-V" (vertical writing
#   mode) versions. Those with only a "-H" version are explicitly
#   shown with the "-H" appended. Those with both do not have a
#   writing mode suffix.
#
# o The character codes found in a corresponding "-V" (vertical
#   writing mode) CMap file are indicated by a "v" appended to the
#   hexadecimal code.
#
# o There may be cases of single CIDs being referenced in multiple
#   encoding points within a single CMap file. These cases are
#   comma-delimited, within the same column.
#
# The following is a synopsis of columns 2 through 32, and provides
# information about character set and encoding:
#
# o Column 2: Character codes for the "H" and "V" CMaps (JIS X
#   0208:1997 character set, ISO-2022-JP encoding).
#
# o Column 3: Character codes for the "RKSJ-H" and "RKSJ-V" CMaps (JIS
#   X 0208:1997 character set, Shift-JIS encoding, half-width Latin
#   characters).
#
# o Column 4: Character codes for the "EUC-H" and "EUC-V" CMaps (JIS
#   X 0208:1997 character set, EUC-JP encoding, half-width Latin
#   characters).
#
# o Column 5: Character codes for the "83pv-RKSJ-H" CMap (KanjiTalk
#   Version 6 character set, Shift-JIS encoding, proportional Latin
#   characters).
#
# o Column 6: Character codes for the "Add-H" and "Add-V" CMaps
#   (Fujitsu character set, ISO-2022-JP encoding, half-width Latin
#   characters).
#
# o Column 7: Character codes for the "Add-RKSJ-H" and "Add-RKSJ-V"
#   CMaps (Fujitsu character set, Shift-JIS encoding, half-width Latin
#   characters).
#
# o Column 8: Character codes for the "Ext-H" and "Ext-V" CMaps (NEC
#   character set, ISO-2022-JP encoding, half-width Latin characters).
#
# o Column 9: Character codes for the "Ext-RKSJ-H" and "Ext-RKSJ-V"
#   CMaps (NEC character set, Shift-JIS encoding, half-width Latin
#   characters).
#
# o Column 10: Character codes for the "NWP-H" and "NWP-V" CMaps (NEC
#   Bungo character set, ISO-2022-JP encoding).
#
# o Column 11: Character codes for the "90pv-RKSJ-H" and "90pv-RKSJ-V"
#   CMap (KanjiTalk Version 7 character set, Shift-JIS encoding,
#   proportional Latin characters).
#
# o Column 12: Character codes for the "90ms-RKSJ-H" and "90ms-RKSJ-V"
#   CMaps (Microsoft Windows 3.1J & 95J character set, Shift-JIS
#   encoding, half-width Latin characters).
#
# o Column 13: Character codes for the "90msp-RKSJ-H" and "90msp-RKSJ-V"
#   CMaps (Microsoft Windows 3.1J & 95J character set, Shift-JIS
#   encoding, proportional Latin characters).
#
# o Column 14: Character codes for the "78-H" and "78-V" CMaps (JIS C
#   6226-1978 character set, ISO-2022-JP encoding, half-width Latin
#   characters).
#
# o Column 15: Character codes for the "78-RKSJ-H" and "78-RKSJ-V"
#   CMaps (JIS C 6226-1978 character set, Shift-JIS encoding,
#   half-width Latin characters).
#
# o Column 16: Character codes for the "78ms-RKSJ-H" and "78ms-RKSJ-V"
#   CMaps (Microsoft Windows 3.1J & 95J character set, JIS C 6226-1978
#   glyphs, Shift-JIS encoding, half-width Latin characters).
#
# o Column 17: Character codes for the "78-EUC-H" and "78-EUC-V" CMaps
#   (JIS C 6226-1978 character set, EUC-JP encoding, half-width Latin
#   characters).
#
# o Column 18: Character codes for the "UniJIS-UCS2-H" and
#   "UniJIS-UCS2-V" CMaps (Unicode UCS-2 encoding, proportional Latin
#   characters). (NOTE: These two CMap files are no longer being
#   maintained. The use of the UTF-8, UTF-16, and UTF-32 CMap files
#   is recommended.)
#
# o Column 19: Character codes for the "UniJIS-UCS2-HW-H" and
#   "UniJIS-UCS2-HW-V" CMaps (Unicode UCS-2 encoding, half-width
#   Latin characters). (NOTE: These two CMap files are no longer
#   being maintained. The use of the UTF-8, UTF-16, and UTF-32 CMap
#   files is recommended.)
#
# o Column 20: Character codes for the "UniJIS-UTF8-H" and
#   "UniJIS-UTF8-V" CMaps (Unicode 15.0 UTF-8 encoding, proportional
#   Latin characters).
#
# o Column 21: Character codes for the "UniJIS-UTF16-H" and
#   "UniJIS-UTF16-V" CMaps (Unicode 15.0 UTF-16 encoding, proportional
#   Latin characters).
#
# o Column 22: Character codes for the "UniJIS-UTF32-H" and
#   "UniJIS-UTF32-V" CMaps (Unicode 15.0 UTF-32 encoding, proportional
#   Latin characters).
#
# o Column 23: Character codes for the "UniJIS2004-UTF8-H" and
#   "UniJIS2004-UTF8-V" CMaps (Unicode 15.0 UTF-8 encoding, proportional
#   Latin characters, JIS X 0213:2004 prototypical glyphs as the default).
#
# o Column 24: Character codes for the "UniJIS2004-UTF16-H" and
#   "UniJIS2004-UTF16-V" CMaps (Unicode 15.0 UTF-16 encoding, proportional
#   Latin characters, JIS X 0213:2004 prototypical glyphs as the default).
#
# o Column 25: Character codes for the "UniJIS2004-UTF32-H" and
#   "UniJIS2004-UTF32-V" CMaps (Unicode 15.0 UTF-32 encoding, proportional
#   Latin characters, JIS X 0213:2004 prototypical glyphs as the default).
#
# o Column 26: Character codes for the "UniJISX0213-UTF32-H" and
#   "UniJISX0213-UTF32-V" CMaps (Unicode 15.0 UTF-32 encoding,
#   proportional Latin characters, some proportional JIS X 0208:1997
#   characters).
#
# o Column 27: Character codes for the "UniJISX02132004-UTF32-H" and
#   "UniJISX02132004-UTF32-V" CMaps (Unicode 15.0 UTF-32 encoding,
#   proportional Latin characters, some proportional JIS X 0208:1997
#   characters, JIS X 0213:2004 prototypical glyphs as the default).
#
# o Columns 28-32: The CMap files for these five columns specify one-
#   byte encodings only: Hiragana, Katakana, Hankaku, Roman, and WP-
#   Symbol.
#
# NOTE: The three "Pro" CMap files differ from their non-Pro
#       counterparts as follows:
#
#                    UniJISPro-UCS2-V  UniJIS-UCS2-V
#       U+2018       12173             8281
#       U+2019       12174             8282
#       U+201C        7956             8279
#       U+201D        7957             8280
#       U+337B       12044              n/a
#       U+337C       12043              n/a
#       U+337D       12042              n/a
#       U+337E       12041              n/a
#       U+FF1A       12101              n/a
#
#       The UniJISPro-UCS2-HW-V and UniJIS-UCS2-HW-V CMap files share
#       the same differences.
#
#                    UniJISPro-UTF8-V  UniJIS-UTF8-V
#       0xE28098     12173             n/a
#       0xE28099     12174             n/a
#       0xE2809C      7956             n/a
#       0xE2809D      7957             n/a
#
#       Note, however, that these "Pro" CMap files are no longer being
#       maintained, and the UTF ones should be used instead.
#
